newsitem.title: USA: Fed adds reserves via 5-day fixed system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed adds reserves via 5-day fixed system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve injected reserves into the banking system via five-day fixed system repurchase agreements on Thursday, a Fed spokeswoman confirmed.
Analysts interpreted the Fed's operation as an attempt by the central bank to provide the market with sufficient liquidity to span the long Memorial Day Holiday weekend.
Analysts speculated the Fed faces an average daily add need of $5 billion to $7 billion during the first half of the new maintenance period.
With the add need growing in coming weeks, analysts said a permanent injection of reserves could come any time during this period, via an outright purchase of bills or, less likely, a coupon pass.
The Fed has performed a bill pass within two weeks after Memorial Day for six of the last seven years, though the add need this year is not so large as to make one a sure bet, analysts said.
The federal funds rate was trading at 5-7/16 percent, below its 5-1/2 percent target rate, when the Fed entered the market on Thursday.
